package application

import (
	"context"

	ident "metaldocs/internal/modules/iam/domain"
)

// A3.3 negative fixture (Rule 1, INDIRECT reference through an alias): the same
// forbidden accessor, never named at a call site.
//
// `extract := ident.UserIDFromContext` is not a call. A guard that matched only
// CallExpr sees a variable being assigned, reports nothing, and then watches
// `extract(ctx)` return the same "" to the same consumer one line later. The
// binding is not a mitigation — it is a laundering step, and it costs an author
// exactly one extra line to perform.
//
// That is why the rule refuses the REFERENCE. Runtime code outside
// internal/platform/authn/context.go may not name the low-level accessor at all,
// in any position: call, assignment, argument, struct field, map value. There is
// no shape left in which "" can be obtained without saying so.
//
// The import is aliased on purpose, so this file also pins that the reference
// rule resolves by import PATH. A rule that regressed to matching the identifier
// "iamdomain" would report nothing here, and the fixture would fail.
//
// See scripts/testdata/guard-fixtures/README.md.
func chargeIndirect(ctx context.Context) string {
	extract := ident.UserIDFromContext
	return extract(ctx)
}
